description: Public-launch readiness audit for CAM Runtime: a written report across nine dimensions with per-dimension verdicts, a go/no-go, and a ready-to-file gap triage.

userStories.title: Scaffold launch-readiness report and audit distribution, onboarding, and external-docs dimensions
userStories.description: As the CAM Runtime maintainer, I need the launch-readiness report created with a machine-checkable verdict-summary table and the first three dimensions (distribution/install, first-run onboarding, external-facing docs) audited, so a stranger's install-and-first-run path is honestly assessed with explicit verdicts and concrete gap lists.
acceptanceCriteria: docs/launch-readiness.md is created and opens with a Verdict Summary table (one row per dimension: dimension name plus a `ready` or `gap` verdict token) that later stories extend. [oracle: file-assert test -f docs/launch-readiness.md]

The distribution/install dimension is audited (private unpublished bun-compiled macOS-arm64 binary via scripts/build-release.sh to ~/.local/bin/cam, no npm bin field, no public channel, ad-hoc re-signing/notarization need) and carries an explicit ready/gap verdict on its summary-table row. [oracle: grep -qiE 'distribution.*(ready|gap)|(ready|gap).*distribution' docs/launch-readiness.md]

The first-run onboarding / cam init UX dimension (for a stranger with no dev setup) is audited and carries an explicit ready/gap verdict on its summary-table row. [oracle: grep -qiE 'onboarding.*(ready|gap)|(ready|gap).*onboarding' docs/launch-readiness.md]

The external-facing docs dimension is audited by COORDINATING with CAM-331 (README build) rather than rebuilding the README here, and carries an explicit ready/gap verdict on its summary-table row. [oracle: grep -qiE '(external|readme).*(ready|gap)|(ready|gap).*(external|readme)' docs/launch-readiness.md]
Every dimension marked `gap` lists concrete, specific gaps (not a bare verdict). [oracle: reviewer-judgment]
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck). [oracle: bun run typecheck]
Tests pass (bun test). [oracle: bun test]
Lint spine passes (bun run check:all). [oracle: bun run check:all]
userStories.notes: New file docs/launch-readiness.md. This is an analysis/audit deliverable (docs-only, no product-code change). Report convention: a top-of-file `Verdict Summary` table with one row per dimension where the dimension name and its `ready`/`gap` token share the SAME LINE (that is what each per-dimension grep oracle keys off), followed by one prose section per dimension. Persisted human-readable .md: no em-dash (travessao), no decorative emoji (global CLAUDE.md rule). Ground the distribution audit in the documented lesson that macOS bun-compile binaries need ad-hoc re-signing off dev machines (notarization for public install). Coordinate with CAM-331 (README) and CAM-332 (brand); do NOT rebuild the README here. Read docs/agent-readiness.md as a prior audit-style doc for tone/structure.

The license / repo-visibility dimension is audited (repo currently private/unpublished; the cam-cli -> cam-runtime GitHub rename is a KNOWN SEPARATE operator step, CAM-329, factored in but not performed here) and carries an explicit ready/gap verdict on its summary-table row. [oracle: grep -qiE '(license|repo.?visibility).*(ready|gap)|(ready|gap).*(license|repo.?visibility)' docs/launch-readiness.md]

The telemetry/privacy stance dimension is audited and carries an explicit ready/gap verdict on its summary-table row. [oracle: grep -qiE '(telemetry|privacy).*(ready|gap)|(ready|gap).*(telemetry|privacy)' docs/launch-readiness.md]
Every dimension marked `gap` lists concrete, specific gaps (not a bare verdict). [oracle: reviewer-judgment]

userStories.notes: Appends three dimensions to docs/launch-readiness.md and adds their rows to the Verdict Summary table (same same-line name+verdict-token convention as US-001). Do NOT perform the cam-cli -> cam-runtime repo/dir rename (CAM-329 operator step); assess it as a factor in the license/repo-visibility verdict only. Persisted .md: no em-dash, no decorative emoji.

userStories.title: Audit versioning/release/update and support-channels dimensions, then write the go/no-go and ready-to-file gap triage
userStories.description: As the CAM Runtime maintainer, I need the final two dimensions audited plus a prioritized gap triage and an explicit public-v1 go/no-go recommendation, so the report closes with a decision and a control-plane-ready list of follow-up issue specs the orchestrator can file on main.
acceptanceCriteria: The versioning / release / update-path dimension is audited and carries an explicit ready/gap verdict on its summary-table row. [oracle: grep -qiE '(versioning|release|update).*(ready|gap)|(ready|gap).*(versioning|release|update)' docs/launch-readiness.md]
The support-channels dimension is audited and carries an explicit ready/gap verdict on its summary-table row. [oracle: grep -qiE 'support.*(ready|gap)|(ready|gap).*support' docs/launch-readiness.md]
The report contains a prioritized gap-triage section that reflects the post-CAM-54 product (claude/codex per-subagent). [oracle: grep -qi 'triage' docs/launch-readiness.md]
The report states an explicit public-v1 go / no-go recommendation with the must-fix blocking set called out. [oracle: grep -qiE 'no[- /]?go' docs/launch-readiness.md]

The report includes a Follow-up Issues section that lists each blocking gap as a ready-to-file issue spec (title plus scope), for the orchestrator/operator to file on main via /cam-issue; non-blocking observations are noted but not listed as blockers. [oracle: grep -qi 'follow-up' docs/launch-readiness.md]
The go/no-go and triage are internally consistent with the nine per-dimension verdicts (every `gap` dimension maps to either a must-fix or a listed follow-up). [oracle: reviewer-judgment]
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck). [oracle: bun run typecheck]
Tests pass (bun test). [oracle: bun test]
Lint spine passes (bun run check:all). [oracle: bun run check:all]
userStories.notes: Closes docs/launch-readiness.md with the last two dimension sections/rows, a prioritized triage, a go/no-go, and a Follow-up Issues section. IMPORTANT (planner rule, CAM-162 defect): this worker story does NOT hand-file issues by writing scripts/cam/issues/CAM-XXXX.json on-branch (that add/add-collides when the branch reconciles with main). Filing follow-ups is a control-plane action performed on main via /cam-issue by the orchestrator/operator; the worker's deliverable is the ready-to-file specs IN the report, which the orchestrator then files. Analysis must reflect the post-CAM-54 codex backend and coordinate with CAM-331/CAM-332 without duplicating them. Persisted .md: no em-dash, no decorative emoji.
